name: Pancreatic Exocrine Secretion and Endocrine Regulation

reference.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology / Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology
clinicalPearls: Acinar cells secrete zymogens (trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, amylase, lipase) stimulated by CCK and vagal acetylcholine
Ductal cells secrete watery alkaline sodium bicarbonate fluid (pH 8.0) stimulated by secretin via CFTR-mediated chloride recycling
Duodenal enterokinase (enteropeptidase) cleaves trypsinogen to trypsin; trypsin activates all other pancreatic digestive proenzymes
Beta-cell insulin secretion: glucose entry via GLUT2 raises ATP/ADP ratio, closing KATP channels, depolarizing cell and opening CaV channels
Glucagon from alpha cells activates hepatic adenylyl cyclase, stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis while inhibiting glycolysis
reference.pathophysiology: In cystic fibrosis, defective CFTR impairs ductal bicarbonate and fluid secretion, causing inspissated proteinaceous secretions, ductal obstruction, acinar atrophy and pancreatic exocrine insufficiency. In acute pancreatitis, premature intra-acinar trypsinogen activation overwhelms protective trypsin inhibitors, initiating autodigestive necrotizing injury.
additionalDifferentials: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency in cystic fibrosis
additionalInvestigations: Fecal elastase-1 assay (<200 mcg/g diagnostic of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency)
Serum amylase and lipase (lipase >3x upper limit of normal diagnostic of acute pancreatitis)
Oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c for endocrine dysfunction
